Application Areas: Structural Analysis of Finitely Presented Groups
Computational Topology and Geometric Group Theory
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Accessibility via G-tree Domination: Establishing bounded complexity for group splittings by analyzing the partial ordering of deformation spaces of locally finite G-trees with finitely generated stabilizers.

Incommensurability via Depth Profiles: Distinguishing non-abstractly commensurable uniform lattices in automorphism groups of Baumslag-Solitar models by constructing and computing the 'depth profile' invariant from their Cayley graphs.

Linear Programming for Stable Commutator Length: Reducing the computation of scl for non-filling curves to a linear programming problem over rational polyhedra, proving piecewise rational linearity by encoding taut surfaces as integer vectors.

Topological Parametrization of Spectral Spaces: Characterizing the homeomorphism type of spaces of reflectionless canonical systems by analyzing the action of PSL(2, R) and identifying orbit spaces as tori or products of disks and tori.
Summary Description: Max Forester is a mathematician specializing in geometric group theory, low-dimensional topology, and spectral theory. His research bridges discrete group structures and continuous spectral analysis. He employs Bass-Serre theory and G-tree actions to classify group splittings and establish accessibility theorems for finitely presented groups. In geometric topology, he utilizes commensurability invariants like depth profiles and trace fields to distinguish lattices in automorphism groups and classify minimal complexity hyperbolic 3-manifolds. Additionally, he applies linear programming to compute stable commutator lengths in surface groups and analyzes the topological structure of spaces of reflectionless canonical systems using Herglotz functions and PSL(2, R) actions. His work provides rigorous frameworks for understanding the structural hierarchies of groups and the spectral properties of differential operators.
